standard_prerequisites.name: Realisation of one inverse system by a filtered complex
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, Lemma lemma-represent-by-filtered-complex, delivered on this card as a context span
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the situation of the statement and the existence of a filtered complex realising the first inverse system, which the proof applies twice.

standard_prerequisites.name: Products in the derived category
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that the product of the two complexes realises the object, which is what allows the two filtrations to be combined on a single complex.

core_obligations: Applying the one-system case twice (proof lines 2715-2722): the author first chooses a filtered complex realising the first inverse system and then a second one realising the second inverse system, both over the same object.

Combining the two (proof lines 2722-2732): the two complexes are mapped into their product by termwise injective quasi-isomorphisms, and the product represents the object because products in the derived category are termwise products of K-injective complexes.

The bi-filtration (proof lines 2732-2735): the images of the two filtrations under those maps provide the two filtrations required, which realises both inverse systems compatibly, and the proof concludes.
proof_roadmap: Map both filtered complexes into their product, using that the product represents the object.
Transport the two filtrations along those maps.
difficulty_reason: The lemma extends the realisation of an inverse system by a filtered complex to the case of two inverse systems mapping compatibly to the same object, producing a bi-filtered complex (statement lines 2705-2713). The proof is a complete argument: the one-system case is applied twice (proof lines 2715-2722); the two resulting complexes are mapped into their product by termwise injective quasi-isomorphisms, the product representing the object because products in the derived category are termwise products of K-injective complexes (proof lines 2722-2732); and the images of the two filtrations give the required bi-filtration (proof lines 2732-2735). The non-formal content is the transport of the two filtrations. The claim is H2.
